headline: Nifty is set to open about 1.3% higher, near 24,280, as oil keeps falling and US stocks jumped. The test is whether it holds above 24,000.

mood.label: Positive
mood.why: The dashboard scores a mildly bullish +24, but only 1 of 4 checks clearly agrees, so most of today's lift comes from overnight news. Overnight data as of 08:46 IST.

key_points.text: GIFT Nifty (Nifty futures traded overnight) was near **24,280** early today, about 1.3% above yesterday's close of 23,960.
Brent crude is at $94, down about **18% this week** on US–Iran deal hopes. Cheaper oil helps India, which imports most of its oil.
FIIs (foreign investors) bought a net **₹7,284 crore** yesterday, more than twice their normal day, and their fourth buying day in a row.
My call: the rise likely **continues at the open**, but it may stall between 24,300 and 24,500. Asia's chip sell-off is the main risk.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: Mostly better news overnight, which supports yesterday's rise.

points.text: The S&P 500 rose **1.6%** and the Dow about 3% after Democrats won Congress and oil fell. US futures are flat now.
Indian shares in the US rose: the India ETF **2.7%**, HDFC Bank 5.6%, ICICI Bank 3.8% and Infosys 2.6%.
The US 10-year bond rate fell to 4.85%, down **0.20 points this week**, and the dollar slipped 0.3%. Both tend to pull foreign money into India.
Korea is down **3.5%**, Taiwan 1.3% and Nasdaq 100 futures 0.6%, as traders move out of chip and AI stocks.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: Continuation at the open, with medium confidence it holds all day.

points.text: For continuation: good news overnight and steady FII buying. FIIs hold only **13.6%** of their index futures as bets on a rise, so many bets on a fall could be closed in a hurry.
Against: Nifty is up about **6%** in two weeks, and domestic funds (DIIs) sold ₹3,712 crore yesterday, which looks like profit-taking.
Professional traders cut their bets on a rise in index futures by **11 points** yesterday, so some fast money expects a pullback.
What would prove me wrong: Nifty falling back below **24,000** in the first hour, or Asia's chip sell-off spreading here.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is improving, but it isn't confirmed yet.

points.text: Nifty is above its 20-day and 50-day averages, and today's open should lift it above the **200-day average (24,004)**, the long-term trend line.
Swings are still a sideways range (a lower high but a higher low), so the price-trend score is only +0.33.
Traders sold many puts (bets on a fall) at 23,400–23,900, which builds a floor. The option score of **+1.26** is the strongest check.
India VIX (the fear gauge) is 15.3, at the **70th percentile** of the past year, so options are fairly expensive. The put-call ratio (bets on a fall vs bets on a rise) is a calm 1.15.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign investors are buying while domestic funds take profits.

points.text: FIIs have bought **₹17,236 crore** so far in November.
DIIs have sold ₹7,783 crore this month. Domestic funds are selling into foreign buying, the reverse of October.
FIIs still have far more futures bets on a fall than on a rise, but that gap shrank by **16,778** contracts yesterday.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Cheaper oil helps most. The US Fed is still a risk.

points.text: Oil fell after Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart talks, but it rests on **hopes, not a signed deal**.
The rupee has gained **1.9%** against the dollar in a month, which makes Indian shares more attractive to foreign buyers.
Six-month US Treasury bills pay **4.25%**, above the Fed's 3.88% rate. This suggests markets still expect a US rate rise.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Yesterday's results looked strong, but I couldn't confirm what analysts expected.

points.text: Apollo Hospitals: profit up **33.5%** from a year ago and revenue up 20.8%.
BSE Ltd: profit up **45%**, revenue up 34%.
Zydus Lifesciences: revenue up 29%, but profit down **25%**. Hindalco reports on 6 November and Tata Steel on 7 November.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: US jobs data, oil and a holiday-broken week.

points.text: US jobs report on Friday at **19:00 IST**. Strong numbers could revive fears of a US rate rise.
If the US–Iran talks fail, oil could bounce fast. Brent has traded between **$72 and $126** since the war began.
There's a weekly expiry on 9 November, then a market holiday on 10 November. India CPI inflation comes out on 12 November.

levels.note: Call sellers moved their wall up from 24,000 to 24,500. A close above 24,500 would mean they gave up; a close below 23,500 would break the floor.

watch.text: IT stocks: the Infosys gain in the US vs the chip sell-off in Asia.
Brent crude. Back above $100 would hurt paints, airlines and oil marketers.
FII/DII figures. A fifth day of FII buying would support the rally.

bottom_line: The night was clearly good for India: cheaper oil, strong US stocks, lower US bond rates and heavy FII buying. The dashboard is only mildly bullish (+24, 1 of 4 checks agreeing), so today's strength comes from news, not a confirmed trend. The main risks are a stall near 24,500 and Asia's chip sell-off spreading.
